method.check_1: Verify source identity, publication venue, title, date, DOI or official persistent page.
method.check_2: Read the exact passage, table, figure, methods, or data field and retain geography, scenario, baseline, unit, defense assumption, and uncertainty.
method.check_3: Corroborate interpretation with an independent authoritative source or reproduce the value from the official underlying data.
method.rule: Corroboration tests meaning; it does not make unlike estimates interchangeable.

checks.evidence: Nature DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07038-3 and article identity verified.
Article horizon for mapped city exposure is 2050; the text and Extended Data Fig. 5 name the three 2070 tide-gauge cases as Galveston Pier 21, Eugene Island, and Grand Isle.
NOAA local scenario data and USACE's HSDRRS description independently show scenario ranges and protection dependence rather than a total-city 2070 inundation finding.
Nature article and official Miami-Dade 2025 Local Mitigation Strategy verified.
Nature reports 2050 additional exposure for a Miami study domain; the county reports a 2070 sea-level planning range relative to a 2000 reference.
NOAA Virginia Key scenarios independently confirm a range of local relative sea-level outcomes but provide no citywide inundation date.
Nature DOI and published article verified.
The main-text paragraph says subsidence can outpace geocentric rise until 2045 or 2070 at three stations; Extended Data Fig. 5 identifies the stations.
The article's Methods confirm tide-gauge and InSAR point/area analysis, while NOAA station geography confirms Grand Isle is distinct from New Orleans.
Nature article and supplementary methods verified.
Abstract and results provide additional exposed area, people, and property ranges under SSP2-4.5 by 2050; Methods specify static connected inundation, elevation/VLM inputs, and 2010 baselines.
NOAA's 2022 report independently supports the need for local relative sea-level projections including vertical land motion, without being used to duplicate the Nature exposure totals.
Nature article, USACE HSDRRS page, and City of New Orleans flood page verified.
Nature's large current New Orleans estimate is explicitly model exposure; its defended sensitivity differs from the undefended analysis.
USACE and city sources independently document levees, floodwalls, gates, and pumped drainage, disproving a literal current-underwater interpretation.
Official 2025 Miami-Dade Local Mitigation Strategy PDF verified.
The Sea Level Rise section reports 10-17 inches for 2040, 21-54 for 2070, and 40-136 for 2120 above 2000 mean sea level at the Key West reference.
Official NOAA Virginia Key scenario data provide an independent local comparison and confirm that baseline and scenario labels must be preserved.
Official NOAA CO-OPS Derived Product API documentation and station responses verified.
API values are 1.26, 2.36, and 3.59 inches per decade at Virginia Key, New Canal, and Grand Isle; reproducing script converts by 2.54 to millimeters per year.
Raw JSON responses are retained with SHA-256 hashes and the output validator checks exact conversion and record end date.
Official USACE New Orleans District HSDRRS page verified.
USACE defines the standard as a 1% annual-chance level of risk reduction and explicitly describes residual risk and design factors.
NCA5 coastal infrastructure assessment independently supports compounding and changing coastal risk rather than permanent risk elimination.
Nature Climate Change 2016 and 2017 articles, corrected 2016 estimate, and replication repository verified.
The 13.1-million value is population at risk under 1.8 meters by 2100 without protection; the 2017 paper separately models redistribution.
IPCC WGII Chapter 6 independently confirms multi-causal, uncertain urban migration and potential immobility; it does not support relabeling exposed population as refugees.
Urban Institute Gulf Coast report and underlying peer-reviewed Houston health/school evidence verified.
Urban Institute Table 5 separates aggregate outcomes from acute, localized institutional strain; Houston arrival and settlement values retain their qualifiers.

The NBER school analysis finds spatially concentrated exposure but no significant districtwide class-size or per-pupil spending increase; the health study confirms substantial needs among evacuees. Together they support a differentiated capacity claim.
